region: Capital and largest city of the Central African Republic
heroText: Bangui is the Central African Republic's capital, a river port on the Ubangi facing the Democratic Republic of the Congo across the water. First-time visitors should see the Notre-Dame Cathedral of Bangui, browse produce and crafts at Bangui Central Market, and day-trip to the dramatic Boali Falls outside the city. Bangui M'Poko International Airport sits close to town, though the security situation should be checked carefully before any visit.

areas.name: Kilomètre 5 (KM5)
areas.text: Kilomètre 5 near the airport is considered the most secure district for visitors, with guesthouses and small hotels used by NGO staff and diplomats.

areas.name: City centre (Avenue Boganda)
areas.text: The city centre around Avenue Boganda holds most shops, restaurants and administrative offices, though it needs extra caution after dark.

areas.name: Riverfront (Ubangi riverside)
areas.text: The Ubangi riverfront has small guesthouses among riverside neighbourhoods, offering a quieter, more local base away from the busiest streets.

airports.name: Bangui M'Poko International Airport (BGF)
airports.search: Bangui M'Poko International Airport, Bangui, Central African Republic
airports.text: Bangui M'Poko International Airport is about 7 kilometres northwest of the centre; arrange a trusted transfer in advance rather than relying on unplanned taxis.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Bangui M'Poko International Airport (BGF) and central Bangui before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Most visitors base themselves in Kilomètre 5 near the airport for its relative security, with guesthouses used by NGO staff and diplomats. The city centre around Avenue Boganda suits daytime errands, while riverside neighbourhoods offer a quieter, more local stay.
hotelIntro: Accommodation in Bangui is limited outside a handful of guesthouses and small hotels; Kilomètre 5 is the most established choice for security and convenience, while the city centre and riverfront offer simpler, more local alternatives.
rentalCars: Self-drive car rental isn't advisable in Bangui; arrange a hired driver or vetted transfer through your hotel or organisation instead.

travelTips.title: Check the situation
travelTips.text: Confirm the current security situation with your embassy or organisation before travelling, since conditions in the Central African Republic can change quickly.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Stay in Kilomètre 5 near the airport for the most established guesthouses and easier logistics for onward travel.

travelTips.title: Transfers
travelTips.text: Arrange airport pickup in advance through your hotel rather than hailing transport on arrival at Bangui M'Poko International Airport.

travelTips.title: Cash
travelTips.text: Carry Central African CFA francs in small denominations, since card payments are rarely accepted outside a few larger hotels.

highlights.title: Boganda National Museum
highlights.text: Boganda National Museum is a key Bangui culture stop, useful for understanding local history, collections and rainy-day planning near the main sightseeing route.

highlights.title: Notre-Dame Cathedral of Bangui
highlights.text: Notre-Dame Cathedral of Bangui anchors the historic and ceremonial side of Bangui, making it a practical stop for architecture, local memory and orientation.

highlights.title: Bangui Market
highlights.text: Bangui Market gives Bangui a concrete street-life stop, with food, everyday shopping and local movement that helps visitors read the city.

highlights.title: Ubangi River waterfront
highlights.text: Ubangi River waterfront adds outdoor time to a Bangui stay, with open space, views or waterfront breathing room between denser city sights.

highlights.title: K-Cinq
highlights.text: K-Cinq is a named stop in Bangui worth keeping on the route when it fits the day's transport, timing and neighborhood plan.

highlights.title: Boali Falls
highlights.text: Boali Falls gives Bangui a greener or more scenic stop, useful when the route needs views, shade, walking space or a slower hour.

nearbyIdeas.name: Boali Falls
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: Boali Falls is a striking waterfall roughly 100 kilometres north of Bangui, a full-day trip that also passes through rural Central African countryside.

nearbyIdeas.name: M'Bali River
nearbyIdeas.label: Nature
nearbyIdeas.text: The M'Bali River area near Boali offers riverside scenery, best combined with the waterfall as part of the same day trip from Bangui.

history.text: The site closest to Bangui is Pendere-Sengue, 800 metres (2,600 ft) from Independence Avenue, where archaeologists and conservation agencies have carried out studies.
The modern settlement of Bangui was founded by Michel Dolisie and Alfred Uzac on 26 June 1889 on the direction of Brazzaville administrator Albert Dolisie.
The colony of Ubangi-Shari received its autonomy in 1958 as the Central African Republic and became independent from France in 1960.
In 1970, President Jean-Bédel Bokassa inaugurated the University of Bangui.
On 25 October 2002, several towns in the country and later Bangui itself were attacked by the forces of General François Bozizé, backed with international support.
Several of its neighbourhoods are in low-lying areas prone to recurrent flooding with severe rains in June and July 2009 leaving 11,000 people homeless.
The agreement was not honoured and the rebels captured Bangui on 23 March 2013, forcing Bozizé to flee the capital.
